statement: A closed subgroup of the full rank-two free profinite group containing the peripheral commutator in its closed commutator subgroup is the whole group. Thus every endomorphism carrying that commutator to a conjugate of a full unit power is an automorphism. For each negative full torus outer involution, the two exact parameter spaces of peripheral conjugators to the appropriate standard negative action are identified by continuous mutually inverse maps. The two-section case uses an element fixed by the other actual section and a prescribed commutator with a cusp reflection; the one-section case uses a pair consisting of an element and its actual involution image. No separate full-generation condition is required.
depends_on: Actual finite covers of the punctured torus and their peripheral homology; full profinite Hopficity for finitely generated groups; D58 actual negative extension, full cusp normalizer, and section classes; full peripheral centralizer and normalizer inside F
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The selected degree-one boundary in a proper finite cover has a second boundary component and a nonzero homology class. Every actual outer conjugator is normalized by the explicit c-power conjugation to one of the two specified cusp reflections.
notes: The proof constructs the standard extensions as full profinite products by mutually inverse generator maps. Every peripheral outer conjugator has a unique representative carrying c0 to c^mu and the standard cusp reflection to c^i v, with i=0 or 1; the exponent is reduced by conjugation with c^((i-z)/2). In the two-class case the tuple (mu,h,w) gives the full basis (h,c^i v w) and satisfies [h,w]=1 and [h,c^i v]=c^mu. In the one-class case the tuple (mu,f) gives the basis (f,alpha_i(f)) and satisfies [f,alpha_i(f)]=c^mu; equivalently an element z outside F satisfies [z^2,c^i v]=c^mu. The boundary test proves invertibility, and the standard extension maps prove the converse. The result is an exact parameterization, without an assertion of nonemptiness for arbitrary full outer actions or a resolution of geometric conjugacy.
